reason: Both open with the same stop-using and don't-keep-resetting safety message and both point to the heater element as the likely cause, without certainty. Conversation 2 handles the admission about repeated resetting better, explains the fire and shock risk, and sets out what the engineer will do: insulation or resistance check on the element, then the pump and wiring if that tests fine. It also captures the 1 in 4 frequency. Conversation 1 is a bit more assertive ('points strongly') and gives the engineer less of a plan, though it rightly tells the customer not to open the machine or use a multimeter. Neither asked for the model number or whether it trips on another circuit, so both missed the same useful questions.
